definition: my self running past the edge of this world, and how little that shows up

settled:
My self does not stop at the edge of this world. The closure runs across every branch, and the one here is a subset of the whole.

Nothing crosses. I can read nothing off the selves on the other branches, so in daily life it changes almost nothing.

But that is only marginally further out of reach than my own past, which I also get at as structure rather than as anything lived, and which also changes very little for me in practice.

The branch boundary is one more seam I cannot cross in a self that is already a run of seams I cannot cross.

I take the picture from Deutsch, The Beginning of Infinity and The Fabric of Reality, read literally and turned on the self. The same source is what moved my test on a belief from coherence to compactness.

title: The Selves On The Other Branches
